items.capacity: Signatory to the July 2023 voluntary AI safety, security and trust commitments
items.fact: Anthropic was one of seven companies (Amazon, Google, Inflection, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI) that the White House said it was convening on 21 July 2023 to announce voluntary commitments. The archived fact sheet read names no White House staff member who ran the process.
items.quote: convening seven leading AI companies at the White House today
items.missing: Official account naming the White House staff who ran the process (not_found in the fact sheet read); Anthropic's own commitment text was not read.
items.notes: Secondary coverage says the commitments have no enforcement mechanism (not verified on a primary page). The same fact sheet says the President and Vice President convened CEOs of Google, Anthropic, Microsoft and OpenAI in May 2023.

items.from: US AI Safety Institute (NIST, US Department of Commerce)
items.capacity: Memorandum of Understanding on pre- and post-release model access and collaborative safety research
items.fact: NIST announced on 29 August 2024 that each company's Memorandum of Understanding sets up a framework for the AI Safety Institute to receive access to major new models before and after public release. NIST's page also states that AISI was re-established as CAISI in June 2025.
items.quote: Each company’s Memorandum of Understanding establishes the framework for the U.S. AI Safety Institute
items.missing: The MOU text itself; whether any pre-release access has been exercised.
items.notes: Only the NIST release was read; press coverage in search results matches it.

items.from: US Department of Defense, Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO)
items.fact: The CDAO awarded Anthropic a two-year prototype other transaction agreement with a $200 million ceiling, announced by Anthropic on 14 July 2025. The ceiling is a maximum, and the announcement gives no obligated amount.
items.quote: has awarded Anthropic a two-year prototype other transaction agreement with a $200 million ceiling
items.missing: Award date (the start date is the announcement date); obligated value; period-of-performance end date; DoD notice of award.
items.notes: A search summary says Google, OpenAI and xAI received parallel $200 million awards; not checked on a DoD page.

items.capacity: Product: Claude Gov models for US national security customers
items.fact: Anthropic announced on 6 June 2025 a custom set of Claude Gov models for US national security customers, saying agencies at the highest level of national security already deploy them. The page gives no price or contract value.
items.quote: custom set of Claude Gov models built exclusively for U.S. national security customers
items.missing: Contract vehicle, pricing and which agencies buy it.

items.capacity: Claude access deployment for LLNL scientists, researchers and staff
items.fact: Anthropic's 14 July 2025 post says that the week before, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory had announced it would make advanced AI capabilities available to over 10,000 staff. The LLNL announcement itself was not read, and no ceiling or contract value is given.
items.quote: will make advanced AI capabilities available to over 10,000 scientists, researchers, and staff
items.missing: Exact LLNL announcement date; contract vehicle and any dollar value.
items.notes: The start month is inferred from 'last week' in the 14 July 2025 post.

items.capacity: OneGov agreement for Claude for Enterprise and Claude for Government
items.fact: GSA announced on 12 August 2025 a OneGov agreement to deliver Claude for Enterprise and Claude for Government to all three branches of the US government for a nominal fee of $1. GSA structured it so other agencies, and Congress and the judiciary subject to their approval, can use it.
items.missing: Current term and expiry (search summaries conflict: Aug 2026 vs Oct 2026, unverified); uptake by Congress and the judiciary; order records.
items.notes: A search summary says the offer was later extended; not verified.

items.from: US Department of War (Pentagon), Secretary Pete Hegseth
items.capacity: Supply chain risk designation of Anthropic and its products
items.fact: On 5 March 2026 the Pentagon told Anthropic leadership that the company and its products are deemed a supply chain risk, effective immediately, after Anthropic refused to drop limits on mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons. As of the latest reports found, a N.D. Cal. judge enjoined the 10 U.S.C. 3252 designation (27 Aug 2026), a D.C. Circuit panel upheld the FASCSA designation 2-1 (reported 25 Sep 2026), and a Pentagon official said on 3 Sep 2026 that Anthropic is still designated.
items.quote: the company and its products are deemed a supply chain risk, effective immediately
items.missing: Status as of 2026-11-12 beyond the reports found: whether the D.C. Circuit rehearing petition or any Supreme Court step changed it; the written designation notice; the statute cited by the Pentagon (secondary coverage names 10 U.S.C. 3252 and 41 U.S.C. 4713).
items.notes: Reason: NPR/AP reports Amodei refused to back down over those limits; the Pentagon statement read gives no further reason. Court items come from AP/NPR (28 Aug 2026), Washington Examiner (3 Sep 2026), and a Taft law bulletin on the D.C. Circuit holding (not the opinion; the 25 Sep date is from secondary coverage). NPR confirms Trump gave the military six months to phase out Claude; the all-agency directive is from search summaries only.

items.fact: In a January 2025 essay on darioamodei.com, Dario Amodei wrote that he had made the case for stronger US export controls on chips to China, and that export controls keep democratic nations at the forefront of AI development. It is a personal essay by the Anthropic CEO, not a company statement.
items.quote: I made the case for stronger US export controls on chips to China.
items.missing: Exact posting day; whether Anthropic reposted it as a company statement.

items.to: US Department of Commerce (Framework for AI Diffusion interim final rule)
items.capacity: Company submission on the AI diffusion rule and export controls
items.fact: Anthropic's 30 April 2025 submission recommends maintaining and strengthening export controls on advanced semiconductors. Its page describes the January 2025 'Diffusion Rule' as establishing export controls on advanced AI chips and model weights worldwide.
items.quote: maintaining America’s compute advantage through export controls is essential for national security and economic prosperity
items.missing: The full submission PDF (linked from the page; not read).

items.capacity: Co-author of Wall Street Journal op-ed
items.fact: page not read: the op-ed itself was not fetched. Anthropic's 30 April 2025 page lists 'Trump Can Keep America's AI Advantage' by Dario Amodei and Matthew Pottinger, Wall Street Journal, January 6, 2025, as a prior position piece.
items.publisher: Wall Street Journal (as listed by Anthropic)
items.quote: Trump Can Keep America’s AI Advantage
items.missing: The op-ed text (its export-control asks); Pottinger's title at the time. A search summary calls him a former deputy national security adviser; not verified.

items.to: US Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP)
items.capacity: Submission to the White House request for information on an AI Action Plan
items.fact: On 6 March 2025 Anthropic sent OSTP recommendations for the US AI Action Plan in six areas: national security testing, strengthening export controls (tightening semiconductor export restrictions), enhancing lab security, scaling energy infrastructure, accelerating government AI adoption, and preparing for economic impacts.
items.quote: build an additional 50 gigawatts of dedicated power by 2027
items.notes: Anthropic's page was read; its July 2025 follow-up post was not.

items.to: Vice President Kamala Harris and senior administration officials (White House)
items.fact: The official White House readout dated 4 May 2023 lists Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, among the CEOs who met Vice President Harris and senior administration officials, and says President Biden dropped by. No Biden-era Anthropic meeting in 2024 was found.
items.missing: Any 2024 Biden-era meeting with Anthropic leaders (none found in two searches); the 21 July 2023 event attendee list for Anthropic (the fact sheet confirms the company was convened, not who attended).
items.notes: Two 2024 searches returned only the Trump-administration meeting with Susie Wiles on 17 Apr 2026 (secondary coverage), which is outside the requested scope.
